fire:
Sift the flour, baking powder and cinnamon into a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the eggs with the oil, then fold the flour mixture into the egg mixture.

Melt the chocolate over simmering water and let it cool.
Beat the butter with the sugar until pale, then stir the melted chocolate into the butter.

Toast the spices in a dry pan until fragrant.
Simmer the lentils for twenty minutes, then add the toasted spices to the lentils.

Mash the bananas in a large bowl.
In a jug, mix the milk and vanilla, then pour the milk mixture over the mashed bananas.

Crush the biscuits into fine crumbs.
Melt the butter in a pan, then combine the crumbs with the melted butter and press into the tin.

Whisk the yolks with half the sugar until thick.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, then fold the whipped cream into the yolk mixture.

Dissolve the yeast in warm water with a pinch of sugar.
Combine the flour and salt, then add the yeast mixture to the flour and knead.

Roast the peppers until the skins blister.
Blend the tomatoes with garlic, then stir the roasted peppers into the tomato sauce.
quiet:
Sift the flour, baking powder and cinnamon into a bowl.
Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line a loaf tin with paper.

Melt the chocolate over simmering water and let it cool.
Chill the bowl in the fridge for at least an hour before serving.

Toast the spices in a dry pan until fragrant.
Store them in an airtight jar away from direct light.

Mash the bananas in a large bowl.
Bake for forty minutes until a skewer comes out clean.

Crush the biscuits into fine crumbs.
Press the crumbs firmly into the base of the tin and chill.

Whisk the yolks with half the sugar until thick.
Serve the custard warm with a dusting of nutmeg.

Dissolve the yeast in warm water with a pinch of sugar.
Leave it in a warm place until the surface is frothy.

Roast the peppers until the skins blister.
Peel them under running water and discard the seeds.
